items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both are true and R explains A: there is a time lag of about two hours between its eastern and western ends, and a single standard time is needed.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on India's latitudinal and longitudinal extent and the Standard Meridian and answer the questions that follow.
"The latitudinal and longitudinal extent of the mainland of India is about 30 degrees each. The southern part of India lies within the tropics and the northern part lies in the sub-tropical and warm temperate zone. The east-west extent of India appears smaller than its north-south extent because the distance between meridians decreases towards the poles."
(i) The longitude of the Standard Meridian of India is: (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'Standard Meridian of India' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: India has adopted a Standard Meridian. (1)
items.answer: (i) 82°30' E (ii) The meridian of 82°30' E, passing through Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh, on which Indian Standard Time is based. (iii) There is a time lag of about two hours between its eastern and western ends, and a single standard time is needed.
items.markingKey: 1+1+1 marks: (i) 82°30' E (ii) The meridian of 82°30' E, passing through Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh, on which Indian Standard Time is based. (iii) There is a time lag of about two hours between its eastern and western ends, and a single standard time is needed.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about India's strategic location in the Indian Ocean is NOT correct?
